blocks.explanation:
The left side has the pattern \(\cos A\cos B + \sin A\sin B\).
That is exactly \(\cos(A - B)\), the fundamental law.
Plan: take \(A = 60^{\circ} + \theta\), \(B = 60^{\circ} - \theta\) and simplify \(A - B\).
steps:
Given: the identity.
To prove: L.H.S. \(= \cos 2\theta\).
Method:
\[\cos A\cos B + \sin A\sin B = \cos(A - B)\]
with \(A = 60^{\circ} + \theta\), \(B = 60^{\circ} - \theta\).

Recognise the pattern
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \cos\big[(60^{\circ} + \theta) - (60^{\circ} - \theta)\big]\]
Why: cos cos plus sin sin is the cosine of the difference.

Simplify the angle
\[(60^{\circ} + \theta) - (60^{\circ} - \theta) = 2\theta\]
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \cos 2\theta = \text{R.H.S.}\]
Why: The \(60^{\circ}\) cancels; minus times minus \(\theta\) gives plus \(\theta\).

Check with \(\theta = 30^{\circ}\)
\[\cos 90^{\circ}\cos 30^{\circ} + \sin 90^{\circ}\sin 30^{\circ} = 0 + \dfrac{1}{2}\]
\[\cos 60^{\circ} = \dfrac{1}{2} \;\checkmark\]
Why: Both sides agree.
